definition: Electromagnetic radiation with wavelengths just longer than visible red light, from about 700 nm to about 1 mm; warm objects such as Earth's surface emit mostly infrared.

A gas in the atmosphere, such as water vapour, carbon dioxide, methane or nitrous oxide, whose molecules absorb infrared radiation and re-emit it in all directions; each has natural and human sources.
The warming of a planet's surface because greenhouse gases absorb the infrared it emits and re-emit part of it back down; on Earth this natural effect keeps the surface warm enough for liquid water.
The extra warming caused by human activities, mainly burning fossil fuels, that raise the concentrations of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
